question: I'm a CS 5th-year student (P-046) with a Math minor and academic warning. I completed 21-355 and 21-356 (Real Analysis I & II). Do these satisfy CS program requirements, Math minor requirements, or both?

domain_contributions.programs: CS degree: Real Analysis courses are typically free electives or advanced math electives for CS, not core requirements. Math minor: 21-355/356 are core upper-level Math minor courses
domain_contributions.courses: 21-355 (12 units, Real Analysis I) and 21-356 (12 units, Real Analysis II) — upper-level proof-based math

key_facts: Real Analysis is central to the Mathematical Sciences minor but is typically an elective for CS (not a core requirement)
These likely count toward the Math minor as core courses
Whether they also satisfy a CS elective requirement depends on CS elective policies (verify)
Double-counting policy: if they count as CS electives, they may not also count for the Math minor
wrong_if_single_domain: Checking only CS requirements might categorize 21-355/356 as free electives or advanced CS electives. Checking only Math minor requirements confirms they are core minor courses. The interaction requires both domains to determine whether double-counting applies.
common_mistake: Counting 21-355 and 21-356 toward both CS elective requirements and Math minor, reducing the perceived remaining course count
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs, CS): 21-355/356 likely satisfy CS advanced elective slots
Step 2 (programs, Math minor): 21-355/356 are core Math minor courses
Step 3 (policies): Double-counting restriction — clarify with advisors whether one or both programs can claim these courses
Conclusion: P-046 needs advisor clarification on double-counting; most likely they satisfy Math minor primarily, and separate electives are needed for CS
